title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the page is part of Grothendieck's study of the moduli M_{0,4} (four marked points on P^1) inside 'Chirurgie des surfaces conformes'. It sets up the octahedron canonically attached to a 4-pointed projective line.

(1) Let I be a set with 4 elements. Let J = P_{2,2}(I) be the set of the 3 partitions of I into two pairs. Let V(J) be the Klein four-group inside S_I, made of the identity and the three double transpositions ('bitranspositions'). It is an F_2-plane whose set of nonzero elements V(J)^* is identified with J: each double transposition determines a partition into two pairs. V(J) acts simply transitively on I, so I is a V-torsor.

(2) Let X be a projective line over C, or over a field k of characteristic not 2, with an embedding I -> X(k). The action of V(J) on I extends uniquely to an action on X by Möbius transformations. This is the classical fact that double transpositions preserve the cross-ratio, so for 4 distinct points there is a unique projectivity realizing each one. This gives V(J) -> G_X = Aut(X) = PGL_2.

(3) Each nonzero element is an involution with 2 fixed points, and these are pairwise disjoint. So the set S of points fixed by some element of V^* has 6 elements, organised into 3 antipodal pairs.

(4) Claim: over C, all faithful actions of the Klein group on P^1 are conjugate in PGL_2. The normal form, in a basis e_0, e_1, is:
- z -> -z, fixed points {0, inf};
- z -> 1/z, fixed points {1, -1};
- z -> -1/z, fixed points {i, -i}.
Hence Klein subgroups V of G_X correspond bijectively to 'octahedral' 6-subsets S of X, each isomorphic to (P^1, {0, inf, ±1, ±i}).

(5) The normalizer Γ = Nor_{G_X}(V) is the octahedral group, isomorphic to S_4. More precisely, when V = V(J), there is an isomorphism of extensions between
- 1 -> V -> S_I -> Aut(V) = S_3 -> 1, and
- 1 -> V -> Γ -> Aut(V) -> 1,
which is identity on V and on Aut(V). Such isomorphisms are determined only up to conjugation by an element of V, i.e. they form a torsor matching the V-torsor I. When I is trivialized (a base point is chosen), one gets an actual isomorphism of extensions.

(6) The next page carries this on. Such data amount to splittings of the extension. These splittings correspond to the four pairs of antipodal faces of the octahedron: the stabilizer of an antipodal face pair is an S_3 complement to V. One gets I ≅ I(V) = F/antipodism. An orientation of the combinatorial octahedron corresponds to a choice of sqrt(-1).

Purpose: a canonical, coordinate-free description of the Klein-group symmetry of M_{0,4}. It identifies the 4 marked points with the antipodal face pairs of the octahedron of fixed points. This links S_I to the octahedral subgroup of PGL_2, presumably for the 'Lego/surgery' description of the Teichmüller tower in genus 0.
errors: The conjugacy of all Klein subgroups, and the identification Nor(V) ≅ S_4, hold over C or any algebraically closed field of characteristic ≠ 2. They fail over a general field k of characteristic ≠ 2, as the parenthetical 'ou mieux sur un corps k' suggests they might hold. For example, PGL_2(Q) contains no S_4: S_4 embeds in PGL_2(k) iff -1 is a sum of two squares in k. In addition, Klein subgroups need not be conjugate over non-closed k. Note that the fixed points ±i already require sqrt(-1). Grothendieck himself notes on the next page that the orientation corresponds to a choice of sqrt(-1).
Notation: 'V(J)^* ≃ J' here means the set of nonzero vectors of V(J), not the linear dual. This is confirmed by the next line, 'élément de J = V(J)^*'. Harmless, but easy to misread.

ideas.what: The Klein four-group of double transpositions acts on 4 points of P^1 by projectivities, preserving the cross-ratio.
ideas.modern_name: Klein four-group / anharmonic group action on M_{0,4}

ideas.what: Klein subgroups of PGL_2(C) correspond to 'octahedral' 6-point configurations (the fixed points), all conjugate; their normalizer is the octahedral group S_4.
ideas.modern_name: Finite subgroups of PGL_2(C), octahedral group

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism of extensions S_I ≅ Nor(V), well defined up to V-conjugation (a V-torsor matching I). Splittings correspond to the 4 antipodal face pairs, giving I ≅ {antipodal face pairs of the octahedron}. Orientation corresponds to sqrt(-1).
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/extension formulation of the S_4 = V ⋊ S_3 structure of the octahedral group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; the torsor-theoretic phrasing is Grothendieck's style
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,4} and M_{1,1} and their automorphisms but not, to my knowledge, this octahedral construction

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, canonical (torsor and extension-theoretic) rewriting of classical facts about the Klein group, the octahedral group and M_{0,4}. It is preparatory material for the surgery/Lego programme, with no new result. The one inaccuracy is extending the claims to arbitrary fields of characteristic ≠ 2.
transcription_corrections: 'formé des bidentité[?]' should read 'formé de l'identité et des bitranspositions'.
'V(J)^* ≃ J': here * denotes the nonzero elements, not the dual.
In the exact-sequence passage, 'J = 𝔓(I)' is presumably 'J = P_{2,2}(I)'.
Struck-out 'quadri groupes' / 'sous-groupes' refers to Klein four-groups ('Vierergruppe').
Margin '(conséquence[?] par G[?])' is uncertain; possibly 'commutant de G' or 'conjugués par G_X'.
'Quand I est le torseur trivial, on trouve un tel iso d'ext.' continues onto the next page with 'revient à se donner un scindage de l'extension'.
